page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.large is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 6455B processor. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 threads, operating at a high clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The compute architecture includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 60 MB L3 cache, backed by instruction set support including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware crypto accelerations. It provides 16.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory (5 GHz), yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio typical of memory-intensive deployments. The instance does not include bundled local storage or GPUs, and it offers a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, driven by the 3.9 GHz sustained clock frequency. Geekbench single-core testing reached 2214.0 points, placing it in the top tier, while single-threaded compression tests yielded 34.49 GB/sec in gzip and 14.72 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, because the instance provides only a single physical core and two virtual CPUs, multi-core and aggregate throughput metrics are restricted. Multi-core Geekbench reached 2683.0, and stress-ng multi-core testing placed in the lower tiers. Memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks recorded 18.56 GB/sec for reads and 17.12 GB/sec for writes.

From an efficiency standpoint, the r7iz.large delivers dedicated high-frequency performance paired with DDR5 memory without requiring allocation of large multi-socket systems. Because it relies exclusively on remote EBS storage and provides 1 Gbps of baseline networking, it is best suited for workloads requiring high per-core execution speeds and substantial memory density rather than extreme I/O. Optimal use cases include single-threaded or lightly threaded enterprise applications, smaller relational databases, in-memory caching nodes, and licensing models bound by core counts.
description: Amazon Web Services r7iz.large is a memory-optimized instance driven by a 3.9 GHz Intel Xeon 6455B processor on the Nitro hypervisor. Configured with 1 physical core delivering 2 dedicated vCPUs, it features 16.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 5 GHz, delivering an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio alongside advanced extensions like AVX-512 and Intel AMX. The instance includes no local storage or GPUs and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark results show top-tier single-core CPU performance, reaching 2214.0 in Geekbench single-core tests, alongside high single-threaded compression throughput. However, aggregate parallel capacity remains constrained by the 2 vCPU limit, resulting in lower multi-core benchmark rankings. The r7iz.large represents a specialized choice for per-core licensed applications, light in-memory caching, small relational databases, and single-thread-bound enterprise services that prioritize clock speed and memory capacity over massive parallel scalability.
